chunks: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, while looking at pigeons in his house: 'There is not a single flutter with which it flutters, except that God repels through it those who enter the house from among the determined evildoers of the earth.'

key_terms.انْتِفَاض: flutter, twitch, shaking movement (of a bird)
key_terms.عُزْمَة: the determined/resolute ones; those with firm evil intentions
key_terms.نَفَّرَ: repelled, drove away, caused to flee

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Abu al-Hasan say about keeping pigeons in the house for protection?
ai.summary: The Imam observed the pigeons kept in his house and taught that each flutter or movement of the pigeons serves as a divine protection, repelling malicious intruders or those with evil intentions. This hadith reflects the traditional practice of keeping pigeons as a form of spiritual protection in the home, a topic addressed in this chapter of al-Kafi. The original audience would have understood this as affirming that even the natural movements of birds kept in a pious household are instruments of divine blessing and protection.
